who: David D. Roberts, historian of modern European intellectual history at the University of Georgia; PhD History, UC Berkeley, 1971.

evidence.says: His CV lists Georgia professor of history, 1988–2003, and department chair, 1993–1998; teaching areas include modern European cultural and intellectual history.
Identifies David D. Roberts as a historian employed by the University of Georgia, educated at Berkeley, with LC authority n78070274.

notes: Institution, period and specialization agree with Mark Clark’s 1997 Georgia dissertation on postwar German intellectual leadership.

who: Dale Vivienne Kent, historian of Renaissance Florence, UC Riverside professor 1987–2009; PhD University of London, 1971.

evidence.says: Records the London PhD in 1971 on Florentine political alignments and her Riverside history professorship from 1987 to retirement in 2009.
Authority heading is Kent, D. V. (Dale V.); source notes identify Dale Kent as author of The Rise of the Medici and Cosimo de’ Medici and the Florentine Renaissance.
Publisher identifies Dale Kent as a scholar of the Italian Renaissance at Melbourne and London and an author on Florentine friendship, neighbourhood and Medici patronage.

notes: London doctorate and Riverside employment during Catherine DeLuca’s 2004 dissertation agree; authority’s initials resolve to Dale Kent.

who: Erin D. Chapman, historian of African American and gender history at George Washington University; PhD Yale, 2006.

evidence.says: GW lists Erin D. Chapman as associate professor, with a Yale PhD in African American Studies and History (2006), and author of Prove It On Me.
Her institutional CV lists service as Brittany Lewis’s doctoral comprehensive examiner in African American history in 2017.
Public ORCID record names Erin D. Chapman and lists employment at George Washington University.
LC identifies Chapman, Erin D. through Prove It On Me, the same book listed on the GW faculty page.
Publisher-deposited Crossref metadata for A Historiography of Black Feminist Activism identifies Erin D. Chapman, George Washington University, with ORCID 0000-0002-5200-8384.

notes: Selected p-29387 has explicit GW employment. The other candidates also match: p-123416 through the book and p-16692 through publisher-deposited article metadata. The latter ORCID’s own public record contains only the name and no career details.

who: Jane Dianne Samson, historian of British imperial and Pacific history at the University of Alberta; PhD History, University of London, 1994.

evidence.says: Institutional CV records the 1994 London history PhD on the Royal Navy and Pacific Islanders, and an Alberta History and Classics appointment beginning in 1998.
LC identifies Jane Samson, author of Imperial Benevolence and The British Empire; its source notes place her in Alberta’s History and Classics department.
Current university directory lists Jane Samson as professor in History, Classics, and Religion.

notes: London doctorate, Alberta affiliation and British imperial field agree with the supervisor record; the appointment predates the 2006 dissertation.

who: Christopher E. Goscha, historian of Vietnam and international relations at UQAM; doctorate, École pratique des hautes études, 2000.

evidence.says: UQAM lists Goscha in History, records his EPHE doctorate defended in November 2000, and lists Phi-Van Evelyne Nguyen’s 2015 doctorate among his supervised theses.
Authority heading is Goscha, Christopher E.; a source note for Vietnam identifies Christopher Goscha as UQAM associate professor of international relations and Southeast Asian history.

notes: Doctoral institution, department and named student agree. UQAM lists Nguyen’s thesis in 2015 under a different title from the supplied AHA 2017 record; retain that discrepancy without treating it as an identity conflict.

who: Yuma Totani, historian of modern Japan and war crimes trials at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa; PhD History, UC Berkeley, 2005.

evidence.says: Faculty biography records a Berkeley history PhD and says she joined the Mānoa History Department in 2008; specialties include modern Japan and postwar war crimes trials.
LC identifies Yuma Totani, author of The Tokyo War Crimes Trial, and cites the Mānoa History faculty biography with a 2005 Berkeley history PhD.

notes: The exact doctoral institution, field and Mānoa appointment beginning before John Porter’s 2013 dissertation support the match.

who: Michael C. Kimmage, historian of the Cold War and US intellectual and diplomatic history at Catholic University; PhD American Studies, Harvard, 2004.

evidence.says: The 2017–2018 completed-dissertation list names Michael C. Kimmage as director of Ryan Carpenter’s Peace Through Strength dissertation.
Institutional CV names Michael Chapman Kimmage, Catholic University history professor, with a Harvard PhD in American Studies in 2004.
LC identifies Michael Kimmage through The Conservative Turn and records his Catholic University history professorship.

notes: Named student and dissertation director provide direct confirmation. The university list gives 2017–2018 and a title ending 1981–1983, versus AHA’s 2017 and 1981–89.

who: Rochona Majumdar, historian of modern India and Bengal at the University of Chicago; PhD Chicago, 2003.

evidence.says: Chicago identifies Rochona Majumdar as a historian of modern India and Bengal, with a 2003 Chicago PhD and graduate advising in modern Indian history and culture.
LC identifies Rochona Majumdar through Marriage and Modernity and a 2007 source describing her as Chicago assistant professor of South Asian Languages and Civilizations.
Identifies Rochona Majumdar, University of Chicago scholar, and links her institutional and personal faculty pages.
The alternative authority identifies R. C. Majumdar as Ramesh Chandra Majumdar, author of The Vakataka-Gupta Age, rather than Rochona Majumdar.

notes: Accept p-102717 and reject p-132007, which is a different named historian. Chicago’s alumni page lists Newbold’s matching dissertation in 2022 rather than AHA’s 2023.
